items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: we have to take into consideration that the George Weins and the people that are supplying so many weeks of work for these people

ctx.x: So rather than to get out of it, I got into it. I said okay, I’m not going to fight the union, I have to help the union, but I have to be a liaison between what the union would like to do and what the guys would like to do. And it’s easier for me to go and talk to the jazz musicians or the rock musicians ‘cause they know me, about a situation, and not do anything unless they want me to do it, rather than having a union representative come in and say, you know, you guys have to do that. I don’t like that. My back…

And with that we’re going to kind of have to wrap up here, but you’ve told us some marvelous things. I think you’ve educated us. I think you’ve given our students and our listeners some things to hold on to, and I appreciate talking to you, and I really like your talking about the feel. Thank you.
